scenarios: arbitrary code in the app's renderer finds no Node, no Electron internals, no raw IPC and the typed bridge only; the Core's address is unreachable and its secret absent; forged approval and browser session refused by the Core; credential values never listed; a child frame has no bridge; a second window with the same preload is refused SENDER_REFUSED by main and audited while the app's window is answered
proof: privileged effects live in main and the Core behind typed requests the app's own top frame alone may make; a compromised renderer or a foreign web contents cannot invoke one.
audit: PARTIAL before: sandboxed renderer, typed bridge, validated arguments; no sender check, no compromise proof.
limitations: a compromise in the app's own renderer may still ask for the person's decisions; socket unreachability rests on CSP and the sandbox; Core refusals are the existing ones.
